'''Seiffert's spherical spiral''' is a [[curve on a sphere]] made by moving on the sphere with constant speed and angular velocity with respect to a fixed diameter.  If the selected diameter is the line from the north pole to the south pole, then the requirement of constant angular velocity means that the longitude of the moving point changes at a constant rate.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Bowman|first1=F|title=Introduction to Elliptic Functions with Applications|url=https://archive.org/details/introductiontoel0000bowm|url-access=registration|date=1961|publisher=Dover|location=New York}}</ref> The cylindrical coordinates of the varying point on this curve are given by the [[Jacobian elliptic function]]s.

== Formulation ==

=== Symbols ===
{| class="wikitable"
|+
|<math>r</math>
|cylindrical radius
|-
|<math>\theta</math>
|angle of curve from beginning of spiral to a particular point on the spiral
|-
|<math>\operatorname{sn}(s, k)</math> 
<math>\operatorname{cn}(s, k)</math>
|[[Jacobi elliptic functions|basic Jacobi Elliptic Function]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Jacobi Elliptic Functions |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/ |access-date=2023-01-31 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref>
|-
|<math>\vartheta_{i}(s)</math>
|[[Jacobi theta functions|Jacobi Theta Functions]] (where <math>i</math> the kind of Theta Functions show)<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Jacobi Theta Functions |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/ |access-date=2023-01-31 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref>
|-
|<math>k</math>
|[[elliptic modulus]] (any positive real constant)<ref>{{Cite web |last=W. |first=Weisstein, Eric |title=Elliptic Modulus -- from Wolfram MathWorld |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/EllipticModulus.html |access-date=2023-01-31 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref>
|}

=== Representation via equations ===
The Seiffert's spherical spiral can be expressed in cylindrical coordinates as

<math>r = \operatorname{sn}(s, k),\, \theta = k \cdot s \text{ and } z = \operatorname{cn}(s, k)</math>

or expressed as [[Jacobi theta functions]]

<math>r = \frac{\vartheta_{3}(0) \cdot \vartheta_{1}(s \cdot \vartheta_{3}^{-2}(0))}{\vartheta_{2}(0) \cdot \vartheta_{4}(s \cdot \vartheta_{3}^{-2}(0))},\, \theta = \frac{\vartheta_{2}^{2}(q)}{\vartheta_{3}^{2}(q)} \cdot s \text{ and } z = \frac{\vartheta_{4}(0) \cdot \vartheta_{3}(s \cdot \vartheta_{3}^{-2}(0))}{\vartheta_{3}(0) \cdot \vartheta_{4}(s \cdot \vartheta_{3}^{-2}(0))}</math>.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Seiffert's Spherical Spiral |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/SeiffertsSphericalSpiral.html |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref>
